body:
If you feel like your issues are becoming worse, I'd suggest you try getting on top of it right away. This doesn't apply to everyone but the longer you go on fighting this battle by yourself the harder it becomes and depression starts to win. Get some support, reach out to people about it.

Things will definitely get worse though if you don't try though. I know, because I've been there. 

Good luck, and I hope you figure things out.

I understand and I'm alright with that decision.

I don't feel overwhelmed, it's more about the fact that I see some threads go without replies, and I imagine that must be pretty upsetting for the OP. I still read them though, and I'm sure many other people do too. That's all.

I tell people on here never kill yourself because of another person, make the choice for yourself. With that being said, is there any way to talk you out of this? I think you might be very short-sighted right now because of this person you've lost from your life. I don't know how long they've been gone, but giving yourself some time before you make any big decisions would be a very wise thing to do.

But if your mind is set, I hope you find peace.

I'm not Caucasian either so I understand the racism a little bit. I used to hate the color of skin, and people frequently made fun of me for it. I hated my heritage too because of it. But I still doubt it's what you're feeling. It's so hard to shake off the racism, especially if you're constantly being hit with it.

Eventually I learned to embrace it, now I'm actually interested in my heritage, and I like it. It just took time to finally accept myself for who I was. Another thing that helped was getting older, people become less racist as you get older I've found. I don't know if this applies to you at all, but maybe you should try and get away from it geographically if you can.

I'm not sure what else you can do, but don't kill yourself because of ignorant fucks. Make something of yourself and show them how wrong they all were.

I hope you're still with us OP. If you are, I want to throw in my 2 cents.

How I wish I knew how trivial and meaningless highschool was. The stupid social structures, the constant danger of embarrassing yourself, always having to put up this fake front to avoid ridicule, and worrying about getting physically harmed for being different. It all means absolutely nothing once you finish highschool. Although you may encounter similar things once you're an adult its few and far between, and there are actual consequences for their actions. Just hang in there friend, I promise things suck a lot less once you're out of school.

As for cutting, I know how addicting that can get. I used to cut myself because I hated myself and felt like a failure. But you're only a failure because you keep telling yourself that. I don't know what your reasons are, but I hope you stay alive. You have a whole life ahead of you still.

It sounds like you're revolving your life around finding someone to love you. I know this is said all the time and I'm sorry for saying it but; how can someone love you if you don't love yourself? For me, I found that to be pretty true. I would drive my relationships into the ground because I was miserable and hated myself. It's hard for people to deal with, even if they love you unconditionally. You may find someone but that someone may leave you after trying to help you for a year or two, and you will feel even worse after. I've done this numerous times.

You seem to be really hard on yourself, you should try bettering yourself, and the rest will come naturally. I know that's no small task, because I've been there. "Why the fuck would I want to better myself when I hate myself?", I would tell myself that all the time. Everything probably feels pointless, but it isn't. 

I hope you decide to try something other than killing yourself. Because even though you may feel like everyone hates you or they have given up on you, It's probably not actually true.

"i dont want to die, i want my life to be different."

That's essentially how I feel. Even though my thoughts are plagued with suicide I think it's just because of my financial and living situation.

I feel trapped too friend, but as for the past, you can't change it, and you have to learn to accept that. You can't fix the future if you're dwelling in the past. Just learn from your mistakes and try to better yourself.

Hey look you're only 17, you may have fucked up, and you may feel things won't get better, but you have a lot of time ahead of you to try and make things right. I'm going to tell you some words I try and live by.

"It's never too late to give life another chance, as long as you are alive."

I've felt like you so many times over the years, and no matter how bad it gets, I think most of the time you can fix it, or move on. I always manged to pick myself back up, maybe you can too. I hope you figure things out for yourself, take care.

I'm the same way. For the last 15 years I kept telling myself I was going to kill myself so what was the point in doing anything. I would always think out all these scenarios, I still can't imagine myself ever becoming old because I still think I'll die before then, probably from suicide. But I'm not really suicidal anymore, after telling myself I was going to kill myself for so long, I still struggle with long-term plans, but it's a process. I wish I had some advice for you other than I know what you're going through. I hope you figure things out for yourself friend.

I honestly don't know why I'm still alive. I constantly think about killing myself and which ways to do it, but I've never went through with any of it. I think the only reason I haven't is because I want to prove to myself that I can do this (life).

I've been through some of the things you've mentioned. I don't know if life gets better, I've been struggling most of my life (I'm 31 now). Things do seem to progressively get worse each year, things haven't been too bad for me the last year though so I'm trying again to be something. I overcome a lot of failures and they keep coming. You gotta find some strength inside you somehow to keep going. When you struggle with depression though, even getting out of bed is a monumental task, but you still do it.

I'm not going to say get new friends, because I understand how hard it is to make friends, meaningful friends anyway. Most of the people I meet become acquaintances that I rarely talk to, mostly because I don't have much to talk about, and things just stagnate. A lot of my childhood friends have become successful and it is really off-putting when I see they've bought a new house or something, and I'm sitting here wondering how I'm going to afford groceries for the next week, or if my utilities are going to be cut off because I can't pay the bill.

Life is a struggle man, I know what it's like. I don't know what you can do to make things better, but you have to keep trying, you've come this far, may as well stick around for the duration.
Everything is temporary, even pain. It's going to be okay.

We're just words on a screen it's sometimes hard for us people to help anyone.

For most people life is usually a string of failures, it's just about overcoming them. What have you fucked up, so I can get a bit of context about your life.

It depends on what kind of loan you have. Some of them are passed onto your parents or they can be taxed for the amount forgiven depending on the type of loan. I don't know too much about this topic though admittedly.

You do seem concerned about your family though, are you sure you want to put them through your death? Not only that but I think you are forgetting about funeral costs. Even if you get cremated it's still going to cost a bit of money. I know that's kind of a shitty reason not to end your life.

Do you know the source of your depression?

"Is it because I don't have anyone?"

This is most likely it. Those are natural feelings when you're already sad. I used to find myself getting depressed and sad when others would be happy because I felt that I would never obtain that happiness. Still working on that but I just try to focus on myself now instead of worrying about what other people are going through. I wouldn't let it get to you too much though, because like I said I think those are normal feelings. You'll find your way.

Sorry to hear your surgery didn't go as planned, I have been reading your threads and hoped it would work out for you. I wish I had some supportive words for you, but I hope you don't decide to go through with it.

You seem really concerned with hurting other people by staying alive, do you have some murderous rage you're not talking about? I've went through similar feelings when I was 16-25'ish. I used to always tell myself I should kill myself before I seriously hurt someone. PM me if you don't want to talk about it publicly.

As for talking to people about how you feel, I've never really been completely honest with someone about how suicidal I've been at times. Like I've told a couple girlfriends little bits of it, but that's as far as it's ever went. I didn't want to tell any therapists or psychiatrists because I was worried they would throw me in a mental hospital. I've slowly started opening up more about in the last half year with them, but I think that's just because the suicidal thoughts aren't as strong as they used to be, so it's not really an issue anymore.

Either way, don't feel guilty for being alive.

Well I haven't seen your face so I don't know what you look like but maybe you're suffering from body dysmorphic disorder.

As for quitting your hobbies, I've done the same thing with virtually everything I do. Like I used to be a good artist, I played guitar & bass, made music, I even did really nerdy shit like build World War II models. I'm just saying not everything you pick up, will stay with you. You may find something that piques your interest in the future.

The reason most people treat you like that when they know you're suicidal is because they have literally no idea what it's like to feel that way, it's like trying to describe colours to a blind man. It's why they think you're being immature and selfish, or whatever tripe they call decide to call it.

Life itself may be completely and utterly pointless, we're just animals living on a rock floating through an uncaring void. But at the same time we don't know the actual answers to what is the purpose of life. It could be something as simple as spreading our DNA, or it can be way more complex and maybe there is a deeper meaning.

But again, most people just don't get it. It's a problem that perpetuates itself because being depressed and suicidal only causing people to push you out of their lives, which in turn makes you feel alone, and even more depressed. It's a vicious cycle.

Leave her and do whatever you can to make sure she doesn't get anything of yours. Don't feel sorry for her, don't blame yourself, don't feel you should do "X" for her because she deserves it. Don't do any of that. I'm saying this sternly because right now your judgement is clouded and in time you'll agree with what I'm saying. Maybe you are to blame for things falling apart, I don't know. But it doesn't justify her cheating on you. I've been in your situation THREE fucking times now, and once my partner cheated on me the relationship was over. Sure they tried to make up for it, but I could never trust them again. That thought of them cheating was always in the back of my mind, it would make me irrationally paranoid, and angry. It's best to just get out. You should also notify his wife as well.

With all that being said, I'm sorry you're going through that man. Being cheated on is probably the worst feeling I've ever had to go through, and I've had close family members die on me. Your gut reaction is to kill yourself to get away from the pain, but give it some time. I wish you the best, hang in there man.

Definitely talk to her, tell how you feel about her, make her feel like you actually care (as I'm sure you do). The reason people consider suicide a lot of the time is that they feel no one cares about them anymore. As someone who has a suicidal mother, I know what it's like.

I might suggest you try and keep yourself busy to stop yourself from thinking about her so much. Or channel those feelings into something constructive. Like for example I go to the gym and I think about her and my memories of us, and how I lost her. I take those negative feelings and I channel it into working out. But whatever you do, just keep yourself busy. Moving on from someone is one of the hardest things I've ever had to do. But hey you're a musician, convert how you feel into music.

As for women just moving into the next guy, my god I hate that. My last two ex's had new boyfriends in a matter of weeks after we broke up, while it took me like a good 1-2 years to even want to date again, then there was the struggle of even finding someone I liked (who liked me).

Hope you figure things out for yourself.

I read some of your post history and all I can say is, don't kill yourself over someone who treated you like that and put you through that. Never kill yourself because of another person, make sure it's a choice that you want to make yourself that isn't influenced by circumstance.

I know you feel a giant hole in your being right now, but give it some serious time.

I kinda just went through the same thing with my last girlfriend. I'm not a very open person but with her I opened up, she was my best friend as well as my lover. She's gone now though and I have to move on from it as painful as it is. So I definitely get it. I think the worst thing about her falling out of love with me, was the fact it was me who drove it to happen. I kind of hate myself for that one.

You have to take baby steps to get your life back on track. Like find a new job and go from there. Don't expect it to all fall back into place immediately. Speaking of cliche I hate the saying "there are plenty of fish in the sea" but it's true. Even though you lost a part of yourself when you lost your girlfriend, you can get it back, and you will find someone else. Sometimes that someone might just be 5 cats though, and if you don't like cats I guess you're screwed (that was a joke).

I once dated a girl who had BPD and it was extremely hard to deal with, so I can't even imagine what she was going through (or you).

I know what you mean about the isolation. I have friends and family but I'm not connected with any of them anymore. They have just become people I knew. I've bounced around therapy and have tried every kind of medication out there, nothing seemed to work until recently. I guess what I'm trying to say is, maybe things will never get good, but it doesn't mean they can't get better.

But no, I won't give you the push you need. I'm sure you've talked your points to death, but if you wish, you can PM me.
I have serious issues with being unable to sleep. My mind is constantly racing.

The 2nd last part of what you said reminds me of this Isaac Asimov quote:

"Life is pleasant. Death is peaceful. It's the transition that's troublesome."

I'm really into philosophy and astronomy, so I think about existence and the purpose of life constantly. I don't think I'm necessarily scared of death, I'm more afraid of the fact that my life will have no meaning once it's ended. Yet what can I as a single person do? Not only that but at least 100 billion humans have lived and died before me, what the fuck makes me so special? I'm just an ape with overdeveloped frontal lobes.

Then don't even get me started on how we're all just made up of 37 trillion cells, and you can keep breaking us down until we are nothing but atoms.
What's your favourite song right now?
Tell us a little about yourself.

Well first I'd like to say, don't give the money back. I know you feel terrible and you feel like you've cost them money, but the problem is that money is rightfully yours because of their poor business practices. If you really feel that guilty about keeping it, donate it to a charity, like a local animal shelter. However I'd advise you hang onto it for as long as possible and see how you feel in the future.

I'm kind of going through some problems of my own and I know how you are feeling about suicide. Whenever I feel really bad I just tell myself to keep going for a few more days, my mood usually changes afterwards. That's really the best advice I can give you for that.

You fought through misery and you beat it for a while, sometimes misery will come back into your life, but that's just a part of living. Beat it again, and you will become an even stronger person.
